problem_statement:
perf(repomap): background the embedding warm-up instead of blocking startup

User-reported: "building repo map... 11s...20s" on the very first message
of every session. Traced it to repomap._semantic_rerank calling
embeddings.ensure_embedded() inline -- which lazily loads a local ONNX
model (fastembed's BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) on first use and embeds the
whole symbol corpus, a cost that's network-dependent (model
download/init) and has nothing to do with the actual repo map build.

embeddings.ensure_embedded_async() now does a cheap SQL check (no model
load) for whether any symbols are actually un-embedded:
- nothing pending (already embedded from a prior run, persisted in
  index.db) -> ready immediately, no thread spawned
- real work pending -> kicks it off in a background daemon thread and
  returns not-ready, so THIS call falls back to heuristic-only ranking
  (fully functional on its own) instead of blocking
- a periodic refresh (5 min) re-checks for newly-indexed symbols without
  ever un-readying an already-warm corpus (stale-while-revalidate)

Caught and fixed a real bug via the test run itself: the background
thread's cleanup assumed its _warm_state entry still existed, raising an
unhandled KeyError in the thread if it was cleared mid-run; made it
defensive (recreate rather than assume).

Only the passive repomap injection (runs on every message) is affected;
an explicit semantic_search tool call still embeds synchronously on first
use, since the model asked for that result and needs it to proceed.
